key_insight: A training-free, identify-then-guide framework (NUMINA) detects attention-heads that encode object counts, derives a countable latent layout, and conservatively modulates cross-attention during generation to correct numeric mismatches between prompt and video.
problem_solved: Text-to-video diffusion models often fail to generate the correct number of object instances specified in prompts; NUMINA improves numerical alignment without additional model training.
method: Identify: select discriminative self- and cross-attention heads that reveal object-localization and counting signals to extract a latent, countable layout.
Refine: conservatively post-process the extracted layout to resolve ambiguities and stabilize object locations and counts.
Guide: modulate cross-attention maps during regeneration/denoising to nudge the model toward producing the specified number of visual instances (training-free).
impact: Enables more reliable, controllable text-to-video synthesis for prompts with numeric constraints, improving downstream editing, data generation, and evaluation without costly retraining.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: identify attention heads → extract latent layout → refine layout → modulate cross-attention during generation
Before/After frames: side-by-side clips showing incorrect vs corrected object counts (e.g., 3 dogs → 3 dogs generated)
Attention-head heatmaps over frames: highlight selected self- and cross-attention heads that correlate with object instances
Bar chart or table: numeric-accuracy comparison (baseline vs NUMINA) across several count ranges
paper_title: When Numbers Speak: Aligning Textual Numerals and Visual Instances in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models
paper_authors: Zhengyang Sun, Yu Chen, Xin Zhou, Xiaofan Li, Xiwu Chen
